Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'rare' (potions.py:1020), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:1022-1028)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

OnUse (protected override, LiquidMemorie.rationale: `CardSelectCmd.FromCombatPile(ctx, PileType.Discard.GetPile(Owner), Owner, new CardSelectorPrefs(prompt, 1)).FirstOrDefault()`, then `SetToFreeThisTurn()` and `CardPileCmd.Add(card, PileType.Hand)` (LiquidMemories.cs:25-30) -> select 1 from `list(player.discard_pile)`, `card.set_free_this_turn()`, `player.hand.append(card)` (potions.py:1024-1028), in that order. MinSelect == MaxSelect == 1, so the ashwater G1 divergence does not arise, and the empty-pile case agrees (CardSelectCmd.cs:390-394 vs combat.py:575-576).

guards.what: N1: the free cost is set BEFORE the card enters the hand, and it is free THIS TURN, not this combat
guards.rationale: Both sides call the this-turn form -- SetToFreeThisTurn, whose sim counterpart is Card.set_free_this_turn (cards/base.py:260-263) -- and the flag is cleared by reset_turn_cost_modifiers at the player's next turn start (player.py:154-155, cards/base.py:265-268). Contrast potion/touch_of_insanity, which uses the this-COMBAT form (set_cost_this_combat, cards/base.py:234-237): two Rare/Uncommon cost potions that differ on purpose, PROMPT.md bug class 29.

guards.what: N2: the auto-resolve shortcut with a one-card discard pile
guards.rationale: Same argument as potion/droplet_of_precognition N1: FromCombatPile auto-resolves when `num <= prefs.MinSelect` (CardSelectCmd.cs:396-399) so the game emits no selection command, and the sim's select_cards picking 1 of 1 returns the same card while the replay driver handles the no-command case explicitly (conformance/combat_driver.py:96-99). One mechanism, verdicted the same at both sites.
